question: Can I change what developers type to create a Swift client instance (from APIClient to AcmeAPIClient)? Is this configured per-language or globally? Does it change import statements too or just the class name?
ground_truth: You can customize the Swift client class name by setting the `clientClassName` configuration option in your `generators.yml` file under the Swift generator configuration. For example: `clientClassName: AcmeAPIClient` will generate a client class that users instantiate as `let client = AcmeAPIClient()`. This is a Swift-specific configuration - you set it within the Swift generator's config block, not globally (other language SDKs have their own client naming configurations). Changing the `clientClassName` only affects the main client class name that users instantiate - it doesn't change module names, package names, or import statements. So users will still import your module the same way, but the class they instantiate will have your custom branded name. This allows you to maintain brand consistency in how developers interact with your SDK while keeping other naming aspects unchanged.

metadata.cited_context: The name of the generated client class. This allows you to customize the class name that users will instantiate when using your SDK.
